title: I am searching for a coffee alternative
content:
I had an in-person work team meeting last week. In the office, they had Bevi seltzer machines. When Bevi machines first arrived at Facebook, where I used to work, I looked down on them. They seemed to be a cost reduction, a sad imitation of The Good Stuff that came in cans and bottles in the fridge. Good Stuff such as LaCroix1 and Ito En tea2.

But this week was different. I noticed that this Bevi had a caffeine option3. After some experimentation, I decided that for the week, I would drink unflavored, chilled, sparkling, caffeinated water instead of coffee. And it was great. Basically none of the coffee side effects.

For several days straight I thoroughly enjoyed a 100-120mg caffeine sparkling water.

But all good things must come to an end. You cannot (yet?) buy a Bevi machine for home. So I am unfortunately now searching for alternatives.

I took a stroll through our local Star Market in search of a replacement. I looked online, too, since we have a weird selection of beverages at that market. I ended up with an assortment of brightly colored cans. Time to do a taste test.

Requirements

In order to swap out coffee for something else, I have the following criteria:

  • no (gratuitous) sugar
  • not sweet (no fake sugar either)
  • no weirdo other chemicals
  • does not taste like jet fuel
  • reasonably priced
  • easy to dose
  • ideally sparkling

We’ll judge based on those.

Taste test

UPDATE Energy Drink: Peach. 12 fl oz. Unclear how much caffeine.

Right out of the can, there is a horrific fake sugar taste. It’s revolting. I guess I missed sucralose in the ingredients when I picked it up. Still disgusting after the second sip and it lingers in the mouth. No thanks.

ZOA Energy Drink: Lemon Lime. 12 fl oz. 160 mg caffeine.

Ever so slightly more pleasant coming out of the can but there is still a chemical sweetness to it. Also missed the sucralose. Gross. No thanks.

SPARKLING ICE CAFFEINE: Citrus Twist. 16 fl oz. 70 mg caffeine.

This time I checked before opening. It has sucralose. Ugh. I guess I was filtering for Stevia at the store. Here goes nothing… ew, absolutely not.

Liquid Death Sparkling Energy: Murder Mystery. 12 fl oz. 100 mg caffeine.

Damn. Sucralose again. Ew. Cherry. Gone.

hi ball energy: grapefruit. 16 fl oz. 160 mg caffeine.

Okay, this is one of the ones I found on the internet first after searching instead of one of the random market finds. It thankfully has no recognizable artificial sweeteners in the ingredient list. I tend to like grapefruit things. Here goes nothing.

It basically tastes like grapefruit LaCroix, which is a win. No sweetener detected. Good news. I like this one by and away the best. Unfortunately, it is expensive, coming in at $3/can.

I intended to do the taste test over a couple of days to avoid over-caffeination, but that was not necessary because most of them were just vile.

Wrapping up and future directions

I also came across Water Joe in my search. Seems there was a man in Wisconsin with similar goals. I want to acquire and sample.

Should I caffeinate my own beverages with liquid caffeine? Seems both less convenient and more hazardous.

Thankfully this is all just because I like the feeling of being caffeinated and not because I am dependent. I will accidentally go several days without drinking something caffeinated and not really notice. I would like to stay that way, so I am avoiding methods that could spike my caffeine intake and accidentally make me dependent.

Please let me know if you have any recommendations…

  1. For a time, I was the “LaCroix oncall”. You could page the oncall rotation and ask what flavor you should drink. I also deputized myself to investigate the occasional LaCroix-related shortage and post internally about it. ↩

  2. There was a period where I was drinking several liters of cold jasmine tea per day. I stopped when I learned that this could do unexpected things to your liver. ↩

  3. Did Bevi have caffeine when I worked at Facebook? Seems like no, they only got it in 2022, and I was Not In The Office that year before I left for grad school. ↩
